hook_text: In 1788 a simple drawing of a ship shocked a nation. What did it show?
clip_script: It showed the slave ship Brookes from above, with hundreds of tiny figures packed side by side in the hold like goods on a shelf. Each figure was a person: chained in the dark for six to ten weeks across the Atlantic, in heat, sickness and fear. That journey was called the Middle Passage. About one in every seven or eight people did not survive it. Before the ships, there were the kidnappings, the long marches in chains, the dungeons of coastal forts. After the ships came the auction blocks, where families were split up forever. Abolitionists printed the Brookes drawing on posters and in newspapers. People who had never seen a slave ship could suddenly see what their sugar cost.
visual_style: A whiteboard top-down outline of a ship slowly filling with rows of small figures; the camera zooms into one figure; then a printed poster version pinned to a wall in a crowd.
pacing: Mystery hook, a slow reveal, a quiet ending.
